analysis.title: Crowded AI, Booming Earnings And A Euro In Freefall
key_insights: Since August 27 the S&P 500 is up 1.3% while the S&P excluding AI names is down more than 5% (GS). The gap is close to the widest since the AI trade began in early 2023, so AI is holding the index together.

GS Prime data shows Mag 7 exposure at around 22% of total US exposure, the highest since their data begins in 2022. Tech was the only US sector net bought by hedge funds in September, with the largest monthly buying since February 2025.

Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth to decelerate from 34% to roughly 27%, the highest consensus growth entering an earnings season on record outside recession recoveries. Deutsche sees growth holding at 34%, about 6 percentage points above consensus.

Deutsche sees semiconductor production and exports across South Korea and Taiwan accelerating again in Q3, with GPU rental prices still rising. DB sees MCG & Tech earnings growth holding around 54% YoY.
SPX is near record highs while long/short appetite has moved the other way (GS). Positioning is not euphoric, which leaves potential buying fuel on the sidelines if earnings deliver.
Deutsche notes the S&P has rallied in Q4 in 21 of the past 23 midterm-election years, with an average gain of roughly 7%. Earnings season has also historically carried a positive bias.
Equity vol has fallen sharply as earnings season arrives. The note suggests using cheaper options to structure upside, for example the SPY Nov 780/820 call spread.
EUR/USD has printed just five small up candles since September 10 and has not moved above its 8-day moving average since the selloff began. The downtrend remains intact.
GS expects STOXX 600 earnings to grow 22% in H2 and SX5E EPS growth of around 20% for 2026, while SX5E is up only about 8% YTD. The multiple has compressed.
Gold has tracked the dollar closely since last autumn, and recent dollar strength has opened a wide gap versus gold. The dollar implies gold should fall further.
GS expects gold to rise 23% through end-2027, with nearly all of the upside attributed to central-bank purchases. The bull case depends on central banks continuing to buy at higher prices.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds net bought tech in September, the only US sector bought, and AI-related earnings growth is holding near 54% YoY per DB.

earnings_insights: Consensus S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth is expected at roughly 27%, down from 34% (consensus estimate, not yet reported).
Deutsche forecasts S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth of 34%, about 6 percentage points above consensus (DB estimate).
DB forecasts MCG & Tech earnings growth around 54% YoY (DB estimate).
GS expects STOXX 600 earnings growth of 22% in H2 and SX5E EPS growth of around 20% for 2026 (GS estimates).

macro_indicators.interpretation: A DB beat of consensus would add support to equities into earnings season.
Nearly all of the upside depends on central-bank purchases.
European earnings growth is outpacing index performance, so multiples have compressed.

trade_ideas.rationale: Cheap equity vol, cautious positioning and a bullish seasonal window into earnings make a defined-risk upside structure attractive.

risk_factors: AI concentration is extreme and the rest of the market is struggling.
The AI trade is now crowded, with Mag 7 exposure at a record.
Gold's bull case depends on continued central-bank buying.
Consensus Q3 earnings growth is a record high for the start of a season, which sets a high bar.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vol has imploded just as earnings season arrives, making upside options cheap.
Mag 7 exposure is about 22% of total US exposure, the highest since 2022 (GS Prime).
Tech was the only US sector net bought by hedge funds in September, the largest monthly buying since February 2025.
SPX long/short appetite is falling while the index sits near record highs, so positioning is far from euphoric.
Trade idea: SPY Nov 780/820 call spread for defined upside into the earnings and seasonal window.
cross_bank_references: Deutsche still thinks consensus Q3 earnings growth is too low, with a forecast about 6 percentage points above consensus.
